title: Count categories
summary: A category is a named group. Counter counts how often each value occurs in a list.
introduction: A category is a named group. Counter counts how often each value occurs in a list. We will use a small example so you can follow each step.
learningObjectives: Use the example to answer a practice question

blocks.text: A category is a named group. Counter counts how often each value occurs in a list.

blocks.code:
from collections import Counter
borrowings = ["story", "science", "story", "poetry"]
counts = Counter(borrowings)
print(counts["story"], counts["science"])
blocks.title: Count categories

blocks.text: The output is 2 1. Story appears twice and science once. This counts events, not the number of different books available.

items: Read the example from top to bottom. Point to the part that uses the new idea.
Add one science borrowing and count again.
Explain what changed in your own words. Check the example again if you get stuck.

blocks.title: A common mistake
blocks.text: Always say what a count refers to: books, events and people are different things.
For more detail later, use this [Data Science further reading](https://www.openintro.org/book/ims/).
